city_center.name: Uptown Charlotte + Charlotte Regional Farmers Market
city_center.landmark: Uptown skyline and the Charlotte Regional Farmers Market on Yorkmont Road; Piedmont rolling country around the metro
city_center.notes: Piedmont NC banking metro. Harris Teeter (founded in Charlotte-area Concord/Charlotte roots, now Kroger-owned) is the home grocer; Publix has expanded into the Carolinas. source: Harris Teeter Carolinas footprint.

featured_frontier.hook: North Carolina sweet potato + muscadine stack -- Piedmont fall harvest brunch, NC being the nation's top sweet-potato state
featured_frontier.photo_cue: Piedmont red clay, Uptown skyline behind, roasted NC sweet potato, muscadine cluster; crisp fall light
featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: NC sweet potatoes (fall, #1 US producer) + muscadine grapes (late summer-fall)

cross_promo.activation: NC sweet-potato + muscadine recipe card, Harris Teeter retailer lockup

audience: Piedmont NC banking-and-suburb families; Harris Teeter-first Charlotte households

languages.reason: Spanish is the leading second home language across the Charlotte metro. Percentage INFERRED (localization pipeline data absent) -- not an ACS figure

cultural_notes: Charlotte is a Piedmont banking metro; Harris Teeter, with Charlotte-area roots, is the flagship Carolinas grocer, and Publix has expanded into the region (source: Harris Teeter / Publix Carolinas footprint; language selection flagged INFERRED)

North Carolina is the top sweet-potato producing state in the US, and apples run August through February in the state's orchards (source: NC Cooperative Extension buncombe.ces.ncsu.edu / brunswick.ces.ncsu.edu; morefood.org fall produce)
Muscadine, the native Southern grape, is available late summer through fall and even lingers into early December in North Carolina (source: discover.texasrealfood.com North Carolina December)
